text: Good afternoon everyone. It's 2 o'clock and I would like to call to order the Standing Policy Committee on Finance for Monday, September 12th. And we're going to go straight to 7.3.1. Discover Saskatoon contract. Mr. Hack.
Thank you. Madame Chair. As outlined in the report, Discover Saskatoon's contract is currently set to expire at the end of 2022.
The administration has been having several conversations with Discover Saskatoon regarding a new contract over the past number of months.
The current contract in mandate between the city and Discover Saskatoon includes a variety of broad provisions such as Operation of a Visitor Center,
advertising to attract visitors from other markets and attraction of special events and conventions that utilize local and city owned facilities.
As seen in attachment number two, Discover Saskatoon is seeking an increase in funding of 50,000 per year for the next three years.
In order to increase the mandate to essentially not only attract visitors to the city, but provide end to end tourism services from attraction, arrival, experience and follow-up.
While Discover Saskatoon certainly makes the compelling case to expand services and transition from a destination management organization to a destination management and marketing organization,
the timing of the requested increase in service levels and funding has several implications.
Most notably, the city's projected multi-million dollar deficit make it difficult to invest in increased service levels at this time.
Continued uncertainty as we continue to recover from the pandemic and a lack of clarity surrounding the key performance indicators the city is trying to achieve through this contract.
As such, the administration has provided several options in the report for consideration.
The current recommendation is to proceed with a one year bridge contract with Discover Saskatoon including a 5% increase to current funding.

The 5% increase in current funding is being recommended in order to recognize that the current inflationary clause in the contract has not been a good tie to the value that Discover Saskatoon provides and has actually eroded the city's contribution over time since it has not kept up with inflation.

The one year contract is being recommended in order to provide additional time for the city administration to work with Discover Saskatoon to develop measurable key performance indicators that can be tied to financial incentives to better understand the link the city's investment has to the desired results.
The 5% contractual increase would result in an additional 15,100 needing to be added to the 2023 budget which would be brought forward to budget deliberations for addition.
With that, I'd be happy to answer any questions committee may have for administration.
Thank you. If it's okay with committee, I think we'll hear from the speaker first.
Okay, I am pleased welcome.
Steph Klobchuk with Discover Saskatoon.
Good afternoon Madam Chair and administration council members.
I acknowledge as well that we are here gathered on 36 territory in the homeland of the meeting.
I thank you for having me today and I'm here to speak to administrations report on the city of Saskatoon's contract with Discover Saskatoon.

I really do appreciate and understand administrations recommendation today and want to thank the city's CFO clay for his time and partnership over the past many months that we have been working to chart a new path.
And I still come before you today to request your approval and consideration of our request of three years through your contract with Discover Saskatoon.
That includes a $50,000 increase year over year for the next three years.
As you have read a nice admission, Madam Chair, my clock has not started. Does that matter?
As you have read in my submission, the scope of work that our organization provides and your city goes far beyond a few annual promotional campaigns and catchy tag lines.

We are your voice across Canada and around the world building partnerships and networks of Saskatoon ambassadors as we create compelling invitations to business, sport and leisure travelers to discover Saskatoon.
In 2019, this equated to $716 million being spent in Saskatoon's visitor economy that represented over 15,000 local job jobs, making tourism when if Saskatchewan's top three export industries.
While we are the voice of Saskatoon abroad, we have a critical role to play here at home related to what I'm referring to as destination management.
One of the ultimate goals of tourism is to increase quality of life for residents and then discover Saskatoon successfully inspires visitation.
We drive economic prosperity, attract human capital and enable investment attraction into our local economy.
In addition to developing strategies that enhance visitation, we must also focus on implementing core strategies for destination management.
The past two years have had a dramatic impact on every aspect of life, including how individuals, businesses and investors think about potential destinations.

It is imperative that Saskatoon enhance our position as a place to live, work, learn and visit if we are to forge a future of long-term sustainability, prosperity and quality of life for our residents.
Doing so requires an investment in our experiential assets and core tourism functions.
Tourism has a significant role, for example, to play in Canada's journey to truth and reconciliation.

While Indigenous people have been purposefully distanced from economic opportunities and our authenticity as the destination requires these voices and stories of this land to come forward through our work with our partners at the Saskatoon Travel Council.
We have an obligation to this work to commit to truth telling through our marketing and destination development initiatives and collaborate on employment opportunities.
We are being called to ask ourselves right now what can tourism do to contribute to the health and well-being of Saskatoon and its citizens.
How can we build a visitor economy that delivers demonstrable, net benefit to our host community, while it also serves our visitors.
We must create a sustainable visitor economy that enables residents local businesses and communities to thrive, flourish and be healthy in every way.
And what does it mean to flourish? There are enormous benefits of using flourishing as an indicator of success.
It encompasses human will-being, financial performance and environmental health. It delivers increased productivity, resilience, adaptability and innovative capacity.
And we are ready to work with you on these indicators for our community flourishing to the lens of the visitor economy.
Our investment in thoughtful destination development and experience development has led to the creation of 23 major tourism experiences over the past two years.
These experiences inspire locals and visitors alike with triple bottom line economics. This is a strategic shift when applied to tourism business.

We must prioritize storytelling and experience development alongside infrastructure because I can assure you it is not a building that drives revenue, but the programming and people within it that does.
I believe that many of you have recently experienced a new lesson value authority grazing dinner with a bunch of sheep in the land.
This creation of that in many other guided experiences is the direct result of Discover Saskatoon's investment and coaching.
Unfortunately, last weekend, Mayor Clark and I did not win the net-boning eating contest.
But this end to have the chance to experience the vibrant, matey culture that we have here in Saskatoon is again another direct result of our investment in work.

In Saturday evening, when I attended the 7 generations Indigenous use summit, I met with an attendee from Paul Tech Northwest Territories who took literally every mode of transportation to arrive to Saskatoon and connect with people in our land.

It is not business as usual tourism anymore. We are in a new pathway globally to understand how tourism can be a force for good for the planet to communities, regional ecosystems and regional economies alike.

I thank you for considering our request and urge you to acknowledge our role as both your destination management and marketing organization and partnership for growth in our community that is needed in the years to come.
Thank you.

Travel trade, media, leisure marketing campaigns and public relations.

hotels, destinations, experience, providers, branches in the area. What is, and you're saying, you believe that Discover Saskatoon needs to have more resources in order to provide for those types of experiences, what is the role of destinations to discover Saskatoon in specifically doing that.

So you met, I'm chair to your worship. The request that I have primarily of committee today is not to acknowledge that we are becoming a destination management organization, but to acknowledge that we have been doing this work alongside the destination marketing work that we are doing.

And so the destination development work that we've been doing for at least the past five years is specifically in the financial investment and the incubation of cultural events, like maybe days, for example, for the past three years we have financially invested in that event to make sure that over the course of its first three years it can become sustainable and competitive and relevant.

In the realm of experience development, we have a 12-step coaching process and business development process that can enable ground up development of brand new businesses, the focus being on experiential experiences, transformative experiences that really get a hands on opportunity for people to immerse themselves in our destination.

So we are physically and financially investing in the business development process of these tourism experiences, we're one of only three destinations in all of Canada that does this work that has the expertise to do this work.
